title: Lower a threshold and watch the trade-off

blocks.text: One precision or recall number depends on a particular decision threshold. A precision-recall curve shows the operating points obtained as that threshold changes. The animation sorts observations by decreasing score and admits them into the predicted-positive set. Initially no row is selected; this implementation defines the starting point as recall zero and precision one.
Build a precision-recall curve at each distinct score threshold for binary labels with at least one positive. Return recall, precision, and stepwise average precision; group tied scores together.

A binary classifier can output a score rather than a yes/no decision. A threshold turns scores into predictions. Precision is the fraction of predicted positives that are truly positive. Recall is the fraction of all actual positives that were found.

Lowering the threshold can recover another positive, but it can also introduce a false positive. Precision therefore need not change monotonically, while recall cannot decrease as more rows are selected. Watch the counters and the selected tokens together. A point on the curve represents a whole decision set, not the confidence of one individual observation.

blocks.text: Connect the picture to the mathematics

blocks.caption: TP counts selected positive labels, FP counts selected negative labels, P is the total number of positive labels, and P_k in the AP sum denotes precision at step k.

blocks.text: Tied scores require special care. A single threshold cannot select one member of a tied group while excluding another member with the same score. The supplied code finds the end of each equal-score group and evaluates the cumulative counts there. Change the scenario to create a tie and observe the combined jump rather than an order-dependent intermediate point.

Average precision here is a stepwise sum of recall increments times the precision at the end of each increment. It is not a trapezoidal area formula and should not be described as one. The function assumes at least one positive label, since recall divides by that count. Scores need not be calibrated probabilities; only their ordering and ties determine this curve. Verify tied-score handling, the initial convention, and AP against the specific definition used by the exercise.

checks.prompt: Three rows are predicted positive and two are truly positive. What is precision?

explanation.correct: Precision divides true positives by all selected rows: 2/3.
